recommendation.basis: On the physical 24 GB RX 7900 XTX, the current automatic low-memory profile completes 208 Ki/128 at 23.623 GiB whole-device peak with 0.361 GiB free. 220 Ki/128 also completes, but peaks at 23.908 GiB with only 81,764,352 bytes (0.076 GiB, about 78 MiB) free, so it is an edge validation rather than a safe operating recommendation.
recommendation.safety_margin_policy: Recommend the largest directly tested point retaining at least 0.25 GiB of full-run approximately 1 Hz observed whole-device headroom; this is an operational recommendation, not a universal allocation guarantee.
recommendation.conservative_200ki_statement: 200 Ki or 200,000 tokens is below the directly validated 208 Ki recommendation and is therefore within the measured context envelope under the same 24 GB low-memory profile.

protocol.device_peak_monitor: rocm-smi --showmeminfo vram approximately once per second for the complete benchmark child lifetime
capacity_pass_requirements: observed whole-device peak is below the physical target device's 25,753,026,560-byte capacity
protocol.safe_recommendation_additional_requireme: at least 0.25 GiB observed whole-device headroom at a directly tested point

notes: The W7900 default-profile rows use 1024 linear/MoE/post/RoPE and 4096 full-attention query chunks because the 48 GB device does not trigger the low-memory policy. They must not be used alone to predict actual 24 GB behavior.

The physical RX 7900 XTX rows automatically select all-768 chunks through low_memory_full_context_24gb. This is why 208 Ki and even 220 Ki can physically complete although the W7900 default 200 Ki and 220 Ki observations exceed the target-card capacity.
Some independent-GPU runs overlapped in wall time. Capacity is per-device and no other KFD process used the measured GPU; throughput remains diagnostic and is not promoted.
No tested run segfaulted. The 232 Ki physical-card run was intentionally not attempted because the same 768-row profile already exceeded the target byte capacity in the W7900 screen.
